key_insight: In LIFT printing, laser energy is converted into bubble-driven fluid motion, making cavitation bubble inception and growth the key bridge between optical absorption and material ejection.
engineering_relevance: Understanding and modeling bubble dynamics across scales can improve donor design, laser settings, and print reliability for difficult-to-deposit materials such as nanoparticle inks, polymers, and bioinks.
method: Review of LIFT donor architectures and how ribbon design/absorbing layers affect ejection
Comparison of thermal-only, plasma-mediated, and coupled plasma-thermal-thermoelastic inception frameworks
Use of multiscale modeling, from reduced-order estimates to interface-resolving simulation and data-driven process maps
evidence_signal: The chapter synthesizes experimental observations and modeling results across time and length scales, using early-stage bubble inception frameworks as initial conditions for downstream growth and jetting models.
watch_item: Predictions depend strongly on the assumed bubble inception mechanism, so unvalidated model choice can propagate error into jetting and deposition outcomes.
paper_title: Laser-Liquid Interaction in Laser-Induced Forward Transfer (LIFT) Printing: A Multiscale Perspective on Bubble Dynamics and Material Ejection
